**Grant Application: CalVIP Funding for Glocks and Fried Chicken (GAFC)**

Sacramento’s communities of color face disproportionately high rates of gun-related incidents, including accidental shootings and suicides. This crisis demands innovative, culturally competent solutions. Glocks and Fried Chicken (GAFC), a minority-owned social enterprise, delivers vital gun safety education directly within these communities, building trust where traditional approaches often fail.

Partnering with Church of Legacy, our multifaceted approach includes the "Gloxsie 21" cartoon IP, engaging youth with foundational safety principles. Our AI education program empowers residents with future-ready skills, demonstrating technology's role in community safety, while direct community workshops provide practical guidance on safe storage, conflict de-escalation, and responsible gun ownership.

CalVIP funding will enable GAFC to expand these critical programs, aiming to measurably reduce accidental gun injuries, increase safe storage practices, and foster a culture of safety. We project significant increases in safety knowledge and community engagement, empowering residents to become agents of change within their households and neighborhoods.

As a minority-owned organization with deep community ties, GAFC possesses unique cultural competency and trust. Our innovative blend of creative media, tech education, and direct engagement positions us as an effective, grassroots leader in violence prevention. This $500,000 grant will amplify our proven, preventative strategies, making Sacramento's communities safer for everyone.
